message.content:
Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-rays demonstrate marked tracheomegaly (dilated trachea) and extensive bilateral cystic bronchiectasis with multiple large cavities, which are hallmark features of Mounier-Kuhn syndrome. The progression to increased number and size of these intrapulmonary cavities indicates worsening disease, necessitating management focused on airway clearance (physiotherapy) and treating acute infections with antibiotics.
